quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Check' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To look carefully at something.
quests.contextSentence: Customs officers ___ luggage carefully at the border.
quests.usageExample: Customs officers inspect luggage carefully at the border.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Check' is a quick look (`check the time`). 'Inspect' means an official, thorough search for faults or safety.
quests.explanation: Natural — thorough official safety checks take 'inspect'.
quests.hint: 'Check' is a quick look (`check the time`) — think of the 'Safety Officer' sense starting with 'I'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Try' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To make an effort to do something.
quests.contextSentence: Runners ___ to beat their personal best at the track.
quests.usageExample: Runners attempt to beat their personal best at the track.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Try' covers casual tasting or testing (`try this cake`). 'Attempt' highlights a serious effort at something tough.
quests.explanation: Natural — bold, difficult efforts suit 'attempt'.
quests.hint: 'Try' covers casual tasting or testing (`try this cake`) — think of the 'Record Climb' sense starting with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Wait' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To stop moving or acting for a time.
quests.contextSentence: The speaker chose to ___ briefly so people could clap.
quests.usageExample: The speaker chose to pause briefly so people could clap.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Wait' marks staying until someone arrives or an event starts. 'Pause' means briefly stopping mid-action to resume soon.
quests.explanation: Natural — temporarily stopping playback or speech is 'pause'.
quests.hint: 'Wait' marks staying until someone arrives or an event starts — think of the 'Video Player' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Thin' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Having little width or body weight.
quests.contextSentence: There is only a ___ chance of rain this afternoon.
quests.usageExample: There is only a slim chance of rain this afternoon.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Thin' applies to paper, ice, soup, or arms. 'Slim' praises an attractive lean figure or small chance.
quests.explanation: Natural — lean figures or narrow margins sound better with 'slim'.
quests.hint: 'Thin' applies to paper, ice, soup, or arms — think of the 'Narrow Margin' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Fat' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Round and full in shape.
quests.contextSentence: Poultry farmers keep birds healthy and ___ on grain.
quests.usageExample: Poultry farmers keep birds healthy and plump on grain.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Fat' can sound blunt or refer to cooking oil. 'Plump' sounds warm and positive, especially for ripe fruit or pillows.
quests.explanation: Natural — ripe fruit and cushions sound appetizing with 'plump'.
quests.hint: 'Fat' can sound blunt or refer to cooking oil — think of the 'Fruit Stand' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Tall' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Measuring a great distance from bottom to top.
quests.contextSentence: Clouds drifted past the ___ mountain ridge at sunrise.
quests.usageExample: Clouds drifted past the high mountain ridge at sunrise.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Tall' fits narrow vertical things like people, trees, and towers. 'High' fits mountains, ceilings, prices, and heights above ground.
quests.explanation: Natural — levels, prices, mountains, and ceilings take 'high'.
quests.hint: 'Tall' fits narrow vertical things like people, trees, and towers — think of the 'Price Tag' sense starting with 'H'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Change' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To stop using one thing and take another.
quests.contextSentence: Many drivers decided to ___ to hybrid cars this year.
quests.usageExample: Many drivers decided to switch to hybrid cars this year.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Change' covers altering clothes, minds, or weather. 'Switch' means swapping cleanly between two choices or seats.
quests.explanation: Natural — trading between two options or lanes takes 'switch'.
quests.hint: 'Change' covers altering clothes, minds, or weather — think of the 'Train Seat' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Start' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To cause something to begin.
quests.contextSentence: The charity will ___ its winter coat drive next week.
quests.usageExample: The charity will launch its winter coat drive next week.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Start' covers engines, classes, and hobbies. 'Launch' means publicly introducing a product, ship, or major plan.
quests.explanation: Natural — rolling out products or campaigns uses 'launch'.
quests.hint: 'Start' covers engines, classes, and hobbies — think of the 'App Release' sense starting with 'L'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Keep' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To hold onto something for later.
quests.contextSentence: Remember to ___ your boarding pass until exiting.
quests.usageExample: Remember to save your boarding pass until exiting.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Keep' means continue holding (`keep warm`). 'Save' emphasizes storing carefully so it is not lost or wasted.
quests.explanation: Natural — preserving items against waste uses 'save'.
quests.hint: 'Keep' means continue holding (`keep warm`) — think of the 'Leftover Cake' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Nice' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Pleasant and considerate toward others.
quests.contextSentence: Shop staff sent a ___ note apologizing for the wait.
quests.usageExample: Shop staff sent a polite note apologizing for the wait.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Nice' is broad praise (`nice weather`). 'Polite' specifically praises respectful words and good manners.
quests.explanation: Natural — respectful manners use 'polite'.
quests.hint: 'Nice' is broad praise (`nice weather`) — think of the 'Guest Manners' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Rude' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Showing poor manners or disrespect.
quests.contextSentence: Interrupting a speaker before they finish is ___.
quests.usageExample: Interrupting a speaker before they finish is impolite.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Rude' sounds strong and emotional (`how rude!`). 'Impolite' is calmer and focuses on breaking social etiquette.
quests.explanation: Natural — mild etiquette breaks fit 'impolite'.
quests.hint: 'Rude' sounds strong and emotional (`how rude!`) — think of the 'Dinner Rule' sense starting with 'I'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Good' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Satisfactory or morally solid.
quests.contextSentence: Every new worker deserves a ___ salary and rest days.
quests.usageExample: Every new worker deserves a decent salary and rest days.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Good' praises quality or morality. 'Decent' means solid, fair, and acceptable without being fancy.
quests.explanation: Natural — good value and fair quality take 'decent'.
quests.hint: 'Good' praises quality or morality — think of the 'Fair Meal' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Sad' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Feeling unhappy or troubled.
quests.contextSentence: He was visibly ___ after losing his grandmother’s ring.
quests.usageExample: He was visibly upset after losing his grandmother’s ring.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Sad' highlights sorrow or grief. 'Upset' mixes hurt feelings with mild frustration or shock.
quests.explanation: Natural — hurt disappointment and frustration fit 'upset'.
quests.hint: 'Sad' highlights sorrow or grief — think of the 'Missed Call' sense starting with 'U'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Angry' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Feeling strong displeasure.
quests.contextSentence: Do not stay ___ over a spilled cup of tea.
quests.usageExample: Do not stay mad over a spilled cup of tea.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Angry' fits serious writing and speech. 'Mad' is informal spoken English (`mad at me`), or British English for crazy.
quests.explanation: Natural — casual spoken frustration takes 'mad at'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ at me" — starts with 'M'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Scared' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Feeling fear or worry.
quests.contextSentence: Many young swimmers feel ___ of deep ocean water.
quests.usageExample: Many young swimmers feel afraid of deep ocean water.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Scared' can go before nouns (`scared kids`). 'Afraid' follows verbs (`afraid of`), and also serves politely (`I'm afraid we're closed`).
quests.explanation: Natural — polite bad-news phrasing always uses 'afraid'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ of" — starts with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Near' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Not far away from a location.
quests.contextSentence: Families appreciate having a ___ clinic during rainy winters.
quests.usageExample: Families appreciate having a nearby clinic during rainy winters.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Near' describes measurable closeness or prepositions (`near the park`). 'Nearby' sits smoothly before place nouns (`nearby shop`) without taking 'to'.
quests.explanation: Natural — before a place noun or at sentence end, 'nearby' sounds natural.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ shop" — starts with 'N'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Far' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Separated by a long space or time.
quests.contextSentence: One ___ cousin mailed photos from across the ocean.
quests.usageExample: A distant cousin mailed photos from across the ocean.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Far' asks simple distance (`how far?`). 'Distant' describes remote hills, forgotten memories, or cool behavior.
quests.explanation: Natural — poetic or remote places before nouns use 'distant'.
quests.hint: 'Far' asks simple distance (`how far?`) — think of the 'Horizon Hill' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Busy' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Occupied with work or movement.
quests.contextSentence: Volunteers remain ___ in cleaning the local riverbanks.
quests.usageExample: Volunteers remain active in cleaning the local riverbanks.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Busy' means packed with tasks or crowded traffic. 'Active' emphasizes energetic movement or live participation.
quests.explanation: Natural — physical energy and participation use 'active'.
quests.hint: 'Busy' means packed with tasks or crowded traffic — think of the 'Healthy Club' sense starting with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Cost' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Money required to pay for something.
quests.contextSentence: Compare the ticket ___ before booking your seat.
quests.usageExample: Compare the ticket price before booking your seat.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Cost' includes total effort or living expenses (`cost of living`). 'Price' is the sticker amount on a shop item (`price tag`).
quests.explanation: Natural — shop tags show a specific 'price'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ tag" — starts with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Prize' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Something given to honor winning or achievement.
quests.contextSentence: Each science fair winner received a shiny gold ___.
quests.usageExample: Each science fair winner received a shiny gold award.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Prize' is won in games, raffles, or contests. 'Award' honors formal merit, service, or film excellence.
quests.explanation: Natural — formal honor for career/art merit is an 'award'.
quests.hint: 'Prize' is won in games, raffles, or contests — think of the 'Film Night' sense starting with 'A'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Job' in the sentence.
quests.definition: Work done to earn money.
quests.contextSentence: Good mentoring helps interns start a strong ___.
quests.usageExample: Good mentoring helps interns start a strong career.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Job' is a single paid position right now. 'Career' spans a person's long-term professional journey across years.
quests.explanation: Natural — decades of growth in one field form a 'career'.
quests.hint: 'Job' is a single paid position right now — think of the 'Long Path' sense starting with 'C'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Find' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To discover where something is.
quests.contextSentence: Use the mall map to ___ the nearest elevator.
quests.usageExample: Use the mall map to locate the nearest elevator.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Find' covers lost keys and surprises (`find joy`). 'Locate' means pinpointing exact physical coordinates on a map.
quests.explanation: Natural — pinpointing coordinates takes 'locate'.
quests.hint: 'Find' covers lost keys and surprises (`find joy`) — think of the 'Map Search' sense starting with 'L'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Lose' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To be unable to find something.
quests.contextSentence: Check the coat pocket whenever you ___ your gloves.
quests.usageExample: Check the coat pocket whenever you misplace your gloves.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Lose' can mean defeat (`lose a match`) or permanent loss. 'Misplace' means temporarily forgetting where you put an item.
quests.explanation: Natural — forgetting where you set an item down is 'misplace'.
quests.hint: 'Lose' can mean defeat (`lose a match`) or permanent loss — think of the 'Pocket Keys' sense starting with 'M'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Send' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To transport something to a destination.
quests.contextSentence: Florists promise to ___ birthday roses before noon.
quests.usageExample: Florists promise to deliver birthday roses before noon.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Send' starts the journey from your hand. 'Deliver' completes handing it directly to the doorstep or listener.
quests.explanation: Natural — completing final drop-off takes 'deliver'.
quests.hint: 'Send' starts the journey from your hand — think of the 'Courier Van' sense starting with 'D'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Put' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To set something in a position.
quests.contextSentence: Waiters ___ fresh napkins beside every plate.
quests.usageExample: Waiters place fresh napkins beside every plate.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Put' fits casual everyday commands (`put it away`). 'Place' emphasizes careful, gentle, or deliberate positioning.
quests.explanation: Natural — gentle, careful positioning favors 'place'.
quests.hint: 'Put' fits casual everyday commands (`put it away`) — think of the 'Delicate Vase' sense starting with 'P'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Pick' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To take things from where they sit.
quests.contextSentence: Students stopped to ___ shells along the quiet beach.
quests.usageExample: Students stopped to gather shells along the quiet beach.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Pick' lifts individual fruit, flowers, or choices. 'Gather' brings many scattered items or people into one group.
quests.explanation: Natural — collecting scattered things together takes 'gather'.
quests.hint: 'Pick' lifts individual fruit, flowers, or choices — think of the 'Autumn Leaves' sense starting with 'G'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Clean' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To remove dirt.
quests.contextSentence: Always ___ fresh berries under cool running water.
quests.usageExample: Always wash fresh berries under cool running water.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Clean' covers dusting, sweeping, or wiping. 'Wash' specifically uses water and soap.
quests.explanation: Natural — cleaning with soap and water is 'wash'.
quests.hint: 'Clean' covers dusting, sweeping, or wiping — think of the 'Dirty Shirt' sense starting with 'W'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Share' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To let others have part of something.
quests.contextSentence: Two roommates ___ the monthly rent right down the middle.
quests.usageExample: Two roommates split the monthly rent right down the middle.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Share' covers feelings, stories, and room cleanly. 'Split' specifically divides costs, bills, or logs into halves.
quests.explanation: Natural — dividing money or food cleanly into shares takes 'split'.
quests.hint: 'Share' covers feelings, stories, and room cleanly — think of the 'Dinner Bill' sense starting with 'S'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Grow' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To become larger or higher.
quests.contextSentence: Warm air causes the fresh bread dough to ___ quickly.
quests.usageExample: Warm air causes the fresh bread dough to rise quickly.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Grow' applies to plants, kids, and habits. 'Rise' moves upward (`sun rises`, `dough rises`, `prices rise`).
quests.explanation: Natural — moving upward like sun, heat, or bread takes 'rise'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "sun ___s" — starts with 'R'.

quests.instruction: Find and trace the synonym that replaces 'Want' in the sentence.
quests.definition: To feel a desire for something.
quests.contextSentence: Travelers toss coins and ___ for sunny skies ahead.
quests.usageExample: Travelers toss coins and wish for sunny skies ahead.
quests.nuanceDifference: 'Want' marks practical daily desires. 'Wish' covers hopes that feel hard, magical, or polite greetings (`wish you luck`).
quests.explanation: Natural — polite hopes and blessings always take 'wish'.
quests.hint: Fits expressions like "___ you luck" — starts with 'W'.
